{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that cleanliness priming would lead to less severe moral judgments than neutral priming among participants exerting low response effort, but that this effect would be absent or reversed among participants exerting high response effort.",
  "design": "mixed, with priming condition (cleanliness vs. neutral) as a between-subjects factor and response effort (low vs. high) as a between-subjects manipulation.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Participants were randomly assigned to a sentence unscrambling task containing either cleanliness-related or neutral words. Response effort was manipulated by instructions: the low effort group was told to work as quickly as possible and not worry about accuracy, while the high effort group was told to work quickly but perform to the best of their ability.",
  "outcome_measure": "A composite score of moral judgments across six vignettes (dog, trolley, wallet, plane, résumé, kitten) rated on a 10-point scale from 0 (perfectly ok) to 9 (extremely wrong).",
  "population_and_setting": "English-speaking adults residing in the United States recruited via Amazon Mechanical Turk.",
  "sample_size_total": 440,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Participants were recruited from Amazon Mechanical Turk and compensated $0.50 for their participation.",
  "analysis_plan": "A 2 (priming condition) x 2 (response effort condition) factorial ANOVA to test for an interaction effect on the composite moral judgment score, followed by simple effects tests.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were excluded if they guessed the study hypothesis or if they responded faster than 675 words per minute on two or more moral vignettes (a measure of insufficient effort responding)."
}
